title: What a Percent Really Is
objective: After this level you can turn "3 out of 20" into a percentage and explain that percent simply means "out of every 100".
summary: Percent means "by the hundred". To turn "3 out of 20" into a percent, divide (0.15) and move the decimal point: 15%. Percents put groups of different sizes on one scale.

cards.headline: "3 out of 20" and "15%" are the same number in different clothes.
cards.body: Percent can look like its own special kind of math. It isn't. It's a way of saying "out of every 100", and once you see that, you can turn any "out of" into a percent.

cards.headline: Percent means "by the hundred"
cards.body: The word comes from the Latin per centum, "by the hundred". It's the same hundred hiding in a century (100 years) and a cent (a hundredth of a dollar). So 15% simply means 15 out of every 100. A percent is a ratio whose bottom number is always 100, and that fixed bottom number is exactly what makes it handy.

cards.headline: Turning "out of" into a percent
cards.body: Say 3 of the 20 cupcakes on a tray are chocolate. Divide the part by the whole: 3 ÷ 20 = 0.15. Move the decimal point two places right and you get 15%. Another way to see it: scale the tray up five times and you'd have 100 cupcakes, 15 of them chocolate. Same share, now "out of 100".

cards.fact: Percents let you compare groups of different sizes.
cards.context: Which tray is more chocolate: 3 out of 20, or 12 out of 100? The raw counts say the second, since 12 beats 3. Percents say the first: 15% beats 12%. Putting everything "out of 100" puts big and small groups on the same footing, a trick this chapter keeps using.

cards.headline: Percent: decoded
learned: Divide the part by the whole, then move the decimal point
